subject: CloudStore compatibility ambassador onboarding
messages:
From: Sandra Li <sandra.li@cloudstore.io>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-02T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot: CloudStore as cold tier for vector fallthrough

Hi Logan,

I lead platform partnerships at CloudStore. We’ve been talking to a couple AI infra teams about providing object-store cold tiering specifically optimised for vector workloads (fast list + range deletes + manifest guarantees). I wanted to reach out to Redwood — we think there’s a nice fit for a small pilot: use CloudStore as an inexpensive cold lane for embeddings fallback from pgvector / Pinecone-style flows.

High-level asks:
- Can Redwood spin up a sandbox project to test list/stream behavior (accessible from our EU/us buckets)?
- We attached our security questionnaire (short) — can your security team return it or point to SOC2/KMS docs we can reference?
- Proposed kickoff: week of May 12; initial 2-week pilot (tech integration + perf/consistency checks).

I attached the questionnaire and a quick architecture note. If this looks useful, happy to put my platform eng (platform-eng@cloudstore.io) and Marco (consultant) on the thread.

Thanks,
Sandra Li
Head of Platform Partnerships
CloudStore

Attachments (2): CloudStore-Security-Questions.pdf, cloudstore_arch_note.pdf

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sandra Li <sandra.li@cloudstore.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-02T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot: CloudStore as cold tier for vector fallthrough

Sandra — really appreciate the outreach and the clear asks. Short answers up front: yes to a sandbox, yes we can run the list/manifest tests you describe, and we can return the security questionnaire (Ben will lead that).

Suggested next steps (proposed timeline):
1) Intake call (30 min) this week — technical owners only to align on S3 API surface + auth.
2) Redwood provides a sandbox project + test harness targeting pgvector fallback + a minimal Pinecone-compatible test runner.
3) Run list/manifest correctness and an eviction/GC exercise (2–3 days), then a perf sweep for list/stream latencies.

Operational asks from our side:
- Can you share any IP allowlist ranges or temporary credentials for the sandbox?
- For production gating we need SOC2 artifacts and a KMS/HSM description — Ben, can you pick this up?
- Vanessa, can you handle partner commercial intake and quick SOW?

I’m looping Vanessa for commercial/SOW and Ben for security/tech docs. For the kickoff call, I can do May 12 at 9am PT if that works.

On Fri, May 2, 2025 at 9:14 AM Sandra Li <sandra.li@cloudstore.io> wrote:
> I lead platform partnerships at CloudStore. We’ve been talking to a couple AI infra teams about providing object-store cold tiering specifically optimised for vector workloads...

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Platform Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sandra Li <sandra.li@cloudstore.io>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-05T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot: CloudStore as cold tier for vector fallthrough

Hi Sandra / Logan — looping in partner ops. Great fit; I drafted a short SOW to scope the pilot and capture billing/PO expectations. I attached the draft SOW (SOW-Redwood-CloudStore-draft.docx).

Key commercial bullets:
- Pilot: 2 weeks technical pilot + optional 4-week extension for additional QA.
- Costing: Redwood covers infra hours; CloudStore provides storage credits for test buckets up to 5 TB.
- Billing/PO: we normally require a signed SOW + PO for any credits over $5k.
- Data residency: we need to confirm EU/US bucket options; please flag any regulated customer concerns.

Security/compliance needs (Ben — internal): please respond to attached questionnaire and provide SOC2 type II report/attestation or an existing assessment URL.

If everyone is aligned, I’ll convert the SOW to signature-ready and send DocuSign. Proposed intake call: May 12, 9am PT.

Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments (1): SOW-Redwood-CloudStore-draft.docx

From: Marco Ruiz <marco@irvine-consulting.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Sandra Li <sandra.li@cloudstore.io>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-06T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot: CloudStore as cold tier for vector fallthrough

On Tue, May 6, 2025 at 08:30 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sandra / Logan — looping in partner ops. Great fit; I drafted a short SOW to scope the pilot and capture billing/PO expectations...

Quick technical note from the consultant side: I’ve reviewed the proposed test harness. Two questions that will affect the test plan:
1) pgvector connector semantics: when Redwood does a fallback read pattern that lists objects and then issues ranged gets, does the connector rely on consistent list pagination (marker continuation) across concurrent deletes? If listings are eventually-consistent in the bucket, we need to add a manifest-layer reconciliation step to avoid missing shards.
2) Do you have a per-object versioning/ETag policy we can use for fast diffing in the test harness?

My suggestion: add a short manifest reconciliation test (5–6 test cases) and a versioning verification. If CloudStore can provide a demo account with object versioning enabled, Ben and the Redwood infra team can run those tests during the pilot.

I’m available May 8 between 10–12 PT for a 30-minute technical sync.

— Marco Ruiz (Irvine Consulting)
Summary: Pilot intake thread to evaluate CloudStore as a cold storage tier for vector fallthrough. Internal owners: Logan (partner lead), Vanessa (partner ops), Ben (security/infra). External: CloudStore platform and consultant. 4 messages over 5 days. Attachments: security questionnaire + draft SOW. Next actions: intake call May 12, Ben to return security artifacts, provision sandbox credentials.
